lh1_mam.text: Hello, cariad, cariad meaning love. Yes, everyone gets one. We are generous with it.
The Snowdon Mountain Railway has run since 1896. It climbs on a rack and pinion track, so it grips like a very polite goat.
We keep hearing a tapping from the old slate wall at night. Dad says it is the coblynau, the Welsh knockers. Nan agrees. I stay out of it.

then.text: Croeso, come in. Kettle's on. Use the table if you like.

else.text: Forty years I split slate up on that mountain. You can still hear it in my knees.
We had a lamp we made ourselves, see. Slate back, peat to light it, a bit of honeywax for the wick. Stone creatures dig like mad for it.
And bara brith, because you can't split slate on an empty stomach. Tea in the fruit overnight. Not optional.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
